questions.text: A shopkeeper marked a price Rs. 3000 more than a cost price. If the shopkeeper allowed a discount of 5 % to the customer it would fetch Rs. 3000 more than if he allowed a discount of 10 %. Find the cost price.
questions.explanation:
Given:

The difference between the two selling price is Rs. 3000

Two different discounts are 5% and 10% respectively

Calculation:

Let the marked price is Rs. x

⇒ 10 % of x – 5 % of x = 3000

⇒ 5x / 100 = 3000

⇒ x = Rs. 60,000

Marked price is Rs. 60,000

According to question

Cost price = Marked price – 3000

= Rs. 60,000 – Rs. 3000

= Rs. 57,000

questions.text: Mahesh and Ram started a business in partnership. Mahesh invested Rs. 3000 and Ram invested Rs. 1000 in the business. Mahesh withdraw 1/3rd of his capital and Ram 1/10th of his capital after 3 months. If profit after 9 months was Rs. 400 then what was Ram share in the profit?
questions.explanation:
GIVEN :

⇒ Mahesh’s initial investment = Rs. 3000

⇒ Ram’s initial investment = Rs. 1000

⇒ If profit after 9 months was Rs. 400

 

FORMULA USED :

Profit = Investment x Time

 

CALCULATION :

⇒ Mahesh capital after 3 months = 3000 – (3000/3) = 3000 – 1000

= Rs. 2000

⇒ Ram capital after 3 months = 1000 – (1000/10) = 1000 – 100

= Rs. 900

⇒ Mahesh’s total investment for 9 months = (3000 × 3) + (2000 × 6)

= 9000 + 12000 = Rs. 21000

⇒ Ram’s total investment for 9 months = (1000 × 3) + (900 × 6)

= 3000 + 5400 = Rs. 8400

⇒ Investment ratio = 21000 ∶ 8400 = 5 ∶ 2

As, investment ratio is same as profit ratio

⇒ Profit ratio = 5 ∶ 2

∴ Ram share in the profit = 400 × (2/7) = Rs. 114.28

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks his product 40% above the cost price and gives a discount of 25% to the customers. At the time of selling the product, he uses 800 gm weight instead of 1 kg. Find his profit percentage.
questions.explanation:
Given :

Marked Price = 40% above cost price.

Discount offered = 25%

 

Assumption :

Suppose the cost price of 1 kg of the product = Rs. 1000

 

Calculation :

∴ Selling price for 1 kg of the product (if he does not cheat) = 1000 × 1.4 × 0.75 = Rs. 1050

But he also cheats by using 800 gm weight instead of 1 kg;

∴ Selling price for 800 gm of the product = Rs. 1050 and

Cost price of 800 gm of the product = Rs. 800

∴ Profit percentage = (1050 – 800)/800 × 100 = 31.25%

questions.text: A shopkeeper sets the 20% mark up for the price of rice and offers 10% discount to the customer. At the time of selling the rice, he uses 900 gram instead of 1 kg and at the time of buying, he uses 1250 gram instead of 1 kg. Find the profit percentage earned by the shopkeeper.
questions.explanation:
GIVEN :

A shopkeeper sets the 20% mark up for the price of rice and offers 10% discount to the customer.

At the time of selling the rice, he uses 900 gram instead of 1 kg and at the time of buying, he uses 1250 gram instead of 1 kg.

 

ASSUMPTION :

Suppose the cost price of 1000 gm rice is Rs.1000

 

CALCULATION :

Since at the time of buying, he uses 1250 gram instead of 1 kg

⇒ Actual Cost price of 1000 gm rice = (1000/1250) × 1000 = Rs. 800

The shopkeeper sets the 20% mark up for the price of rice and offers 10% discount to the customer

⇒ Selling price of 1000 gm rice = 1000 × 1.2 × 0.9 = Rs. 1080

But he uses 900 gram instead of 1 kg at the time of selling the rice

⇒ Rs. 1080 is the selling price of 900 gm rice

⇒ Actual Selling price of 1000 gm rice = (1080/900) × 1000 = Rs. 1200

∴ Profit percentage = (1200 – 800)/ 800 = 50%

questions.text: A sold an article at a loss of 16% to B, B sold this article to C at a profit of 50%. If C bought it from B at a price of Rs. 4,032, what would be the profit or loss earned by A if he would sell the article to B at price B sold it to C?
questions.explanation:
Let the cost price at which A bought be x.

A sold it to B with a loss of 16%

∴ SP1 = 84x/100

B sold it to C at a profit of 50%

∴ SP2 = 150SP1/100 = 4032

4032 = (150x/100) × (84/100)

∴ x = Rs. 3,200

Now, if SP1 = Rs. 4,032 then there would be profit

Profit % = [(4032 - 3200)/3200] × 100 = 26%

Profit % = 26%

questions.text: If a shopkeeper allows a discount of 20% on the shirt priced Rs x. Due to the decreased sale, he further allows a discount of 20% on the shirt. As the sales of the shirt increased, he increased its market price by ‘y’ %. If the difference of the original marked price and selling price in all three cases are in the ratio 5 : 9 : 5, what is the value of y?
questions.explanation:
Original marked price = x

⇒ Selling price after giving 20% discount = (100 – 20) /100 × x = 0.8x

⇒ Difference between original marked price and selling price = x – 0.8x = 0.2x

⇒ Selling price after giving further 20% discount = (100 – 20) /100 × 0.8x = 0.64x

⇒ Difference between original marked price and selling price = x – 0.64x = 0.36x

⇒ Selling price after increasing the price by y% = (100 + y) /100 × 0.64x = (1 + 0.01y) × 0.64x = 0.64x + 0.0064xy

⇒ Difference between original marked price and selling price = x – 0.64x – 0.0064xy = 0.36x – 0.0064xy

Given, they are in the ratio, 5 : 9 : 5

∴ 0.2x / (0.36x – 0.0064xy) = 5/5 =1

⇒ 0.2x = 0.36x – 0.0064xy

⇒ 0.0064xy = 0.16x

⇒ y = 0.16/ 0.0064 = 25

∴ y = 25

questions.text: In a Diwali sale a branded phone of Rs. 15000 was offered at 20% discount by amazon. Raj availed this offer and got an additional 10% discount by paying through credit card. After that, he purchased a screen guard and headphones by spending 5% of the purchased price. At what price he should sell this phone to John with the accessories he had bought to get a loss of 25%?
questions.explanation:
Final price of Phone = 15000 × (80/100) × (90/100) = Rs. 10,800

Price of screen guard = 10800 × (5/100) = Rs. 540

total amount = 10800 + 540 = Rs. 11340

To ensure a loss of 25% he should sell at

SP = 11340 × (75/100) = Rs. 8505

∴ Selling price to John will be Rs. 8505

questions.text: Gaurav started a business of construction by investing Rs. 5,00,000. After 10 months, Ritesh joins him with the amount of Rs. 2,50,000. If at the end of 2 years, the company makes the profit of Rs. 77,500. The share of Gaurav is Rs. _______ more than the share of Ritesh.
questions.explanation:
Investment of Gaurav = Rs. 5,00,000

Period of investment(Till earning of profit) = 2 years = 24 months

Investment of Ritesh = Rs. 2,50,000

Period of investment(Till earning of profit) = 14 month

∵ Share of profit is proportional to the time period and the amount invested

For the respective ratio,

Amount invested by Gaurav × Time period ∶ Amount invested by Ritesh × Time period

⇒ 500000 × 24 ∶ 250000 × 14

⇒ 24 ∶ 7

For profit sharing,

Profit of Gaurav = [24/(24 + 7) ] × 77500 = Rs.60,000

Profit of Ritesh = 77500 - 60000 = Rs.17,500

Difference in earning = 60000 - 17500 = Rs. 42,500

∴ The share of Gaurav is Rs. Rs. 42,500 more than the share of Ritesh

Shortcut Trick

Amount invested by Gaurav × Time period ∶ Amount invested by Ritesh × Time period

⇒ 500000 × 24 ∶ 250000 × 14

⇒ 24 ∶ 7

⇒ Difference in earning = (24 - 7)/31 × 77500 = Rs. 42,500

questions.text: Rajan has divided all his money in such a way that 45% of total amount goes to Rajan's wife, 30% of the remaining money goes to Rajan's two daughter and remaining amount goes for charity. If the amount for the charity is Rs. 96250, the difference of the amount get by wife and one daughter is?
questions.explanation:
Let assume, total amount Rajan had = Rs. x

45% of the total amount gain by his wife;

⇒ Part of wife = 45% of total amount = 45% of x = 0.45x

Remaining money = total amount – 0.45x

⇒ Amount = x – 0.45x = 0.55x

Amount gain by two daughters = 30% of amount

⇒ Amount gain by 2 daughters = 30% of 0.55x = (0.30 × 0.55) x = 0.165x

Amount remaining after daughters' distribution = 0.55x – 0.165x = 0.385x

⇒ Amount for charity = 0.385x 

⇒ Charity amount = Rs. 96250

⇒ 0.385x = 96250

⇒ x = Rs. 250000

Amount receive by wife = 45% of 250000 = Rs. 112500

Amount receive by each daughter = (250000 × 0.165)/2 = Rs. 20625

∴ Difference in amount = 112500 - 20625 = Rs. 91875
